summary: Iteration 55: CRM bug fixes verification. Backend fixes (Outstanding endpoint, JV per-line math, Sundry Debtor filter, Days Overdue, fy_start_str fix, payment-behavior, targets) all PASS — 8/8 pytest tests + curl spot-check confirms 4 Sundry Debtors, no creditors, Krishna jv_credit=-4243, oldest_invoice_days populated (194/348/350/399). HOWEVER the frontend has a CRITICAL regression: CRM page crashes immediately with 'ReferenceError: SortTh is not defined' on the default Targets tab — the SortTh component is defined locally inside the outstanding tab IIFE (line 352) but is also used inside the targets tab block (lines 591-596) where it is OUT OF SCOPE. This blocks ALL frontend testing of the CRM page (Targets, Outstanding, Payment Behaviour tabs are unreachable).

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught ReferenceError: SortTh is not defined. SortTh is declared inside the outstanding-tab IIFE (line 352, scoped to that closure) but is also rendered inside the targets-tab block at lines 591-596 where it is not in scope. Since useState defaults activeTab='targets' (line 12), the page crashes on every CRM load — the dev runtime overlay shows 'Uncaught runtime errors: SortTh is not defined' and no CRM content is rendered. crm-page testid is never present. This is a hard regression introduced with the sticky/sortable headers refactor.

action_items: FIX CRITICAL: Move SortTh component definition out of the outstanding-tab IIFE (currently lines 347-368) and define it at the top of the CustomerCRM functional component (after the state hooks, before the JSX return), OR redefine SortTh inside the targets-tab block. Same applies if Outstanding-tab is hidden via FY-completed branch. The current code crashes the page whenever activeTab='targets' (default) before any tab interaction.

After fix, retest: (a) /crm loads without React error, (b) Targets tab default render shows sortable headers and clicking 'Customer Name' / 'Target' / 'Achievement %' changes order, (c) Outstanding tab thead remains sticky during tbody scroll inside max-h-[calc(100vh-340px)] wrapper, (d) Payment Behaviour tab thead engages sticky inside the new max-h wrapper added at line 883.
critical_code_review_comments: Component scoping bug: SortTh in CustomerCRM.js line 352 is a function-component declared inside an IIFE bound to activeTab==='outstanding'. It is referenced from the activeTab==='targets' branch (lines 591-596) where the IIFE has not run, hence ReferenceError. This was missed during the sortable-header refactor.
Both Outstanding and Targets tabs share the same sortField/sortDir state but each has its own .sort() block — fine, but SortTh duplication / lifting needs to handle both handlers.

Backend customers.py outstanding endpoint correctly uses get_jv_party_amount for line-by-line JV DR/CR parsing, returns small per-line jv_credit (-4243 for Krishna), filters to Sundry Debtors only, and populates oldest_invoice_days by bypassing FY-filter for invoice age (verified via curl).

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: During the recent sortable-header refactor, the developer extracted a SortTh inline component inside an IIFE only invoked when activeTab==='outstanding' (line 347 onwards). When activeTab==='targets' (the initial state), React renders the targets branch which references <SortTh /> at lines 591-596. JavaScript closure scoping means SortTh is undefined in the targets render scope, throwing ReferenceError before any DOM mounts. Reproduction: open /crm with admin login — page is blank with the dev error overlay. Mitigation: Define SortTh once at the component top level (between state hooks and return), parameterised by handleSort (or pass sortField/sortDir/setSortField/setSortDir as props). Each tab can wrap its own .sort() logic but reuse the single SortTh.
